.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r10/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (delivery profile: shaped 0.6/0.2/0.2 behind zero-weight gates and functional floor; verdict/evidence standard; 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass')
evidence: STATIC ANALYSIS (no inversion found): (1) Policy: tests/scoring.toml gates render=0.0/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05; scoring.toml and tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean). score.py:41 gates_passed = all(score>0.0); :47-48 reward = weighted only if gates and floors pass, else 0.0; test.sh:835-849 skips the scored suite on gate failure (exit 1) and writes plain zero on any other score.py failure. Reward is a non-negative weighted mean, so it is monotone non-decreasing in every criterion score; the only discontinuities (gate, functional floor) are themselves monotone (more function never lowers reward). (2) Function dominates: functional 43 criteria, total weight 58.5, max single share 2.5/58.5=4.3%, min 0.5/58.5=0.85%; highest-weight rows (hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private 2.5; hro_refused_put_back, undo/bulk/thread rows 2) are the brief's stated hard parts (instruction.md paragraphs 2-5; hireops_rules.md sections 3 'Two people at once', 'Moving several together', 'Undo', section 5). No structural/craft row outweighs a core functional row. Polish (5 rows, weight 12) is behavioural (live-update preservation, earlier-page anchoring, failed send, session-end drafts), and its two heaviest rows (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread, weight 3 each) are explicitly 0 if no live update arrives, so an app without live updates cannot farm them. Visual is 5 equal 1.2-weight likert rows with anchors (0.2 cap). (3) Gates do not penalise a stronger app: render gate (wrong password stays signed out, correct sign-in shows workspace) and constraints gate (Recruiter UI job+candidate seen by Observer in an independent context) are both direct brief requirements (hireops_rules.md:11-23, 27-36; instruction.md account list); a better conforming app passes them. Every scored prompt restates the browser gate so a static/dead shell gets binary 0 / Likert 1 (normalised 0). (4) Controls prevent vacuous credit: every refusal row names a same-kind positive control (e.g. hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_undo_conflict), and the functional prompt says 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'; so a dead or permissive app cannot outscore a correct one on refusals. hro_candidate_private and hro_candidate_no_staff are 0 if the candidate receives none of their own data. (5) Adversarial probes tried: (a) weak 'persistent CRUD with nice styling' app: passes gates; hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 + hro_restart 1.5 = 3.5/58.5 = 0.060 > floor 0.05, so it can collect visual (<=0.2) and possibly hro_pol_earlier_place/hro_pol_failed_send only if paging and messaging work. Estimated ~0.24-0.29 vs ~0.29 for an app with functional 0.40 and crude visuals (likert 2 ~0.05). This is a near-tie, not a clear inversion, and it stems solely from the template-controlled 0.6/0.2/0.2 + 0.05 floor policy (identical to template; must not be altered per AGENTS.md). Recorded as an observation for the lead, not a task defect. (b) Breadth-dependence: hro_activity requires a line for every performed action, so an app lacking undo/bulk has fewer lines to get right; but missing those features costs ~10 weight units (hro_bulk_move 1.5, hro_bulk_all_or_none 2, hro_bulk_places 1.5, hro_undo_restores 2, hro_undo_conflict 2, hro_undo_once 1) vs 1 for activity, so net ranking stays monotone. hro_activity_refusals (0.5) is vacuous for an app that refuses nothing, but such an app loses every refusal row. (c) Conforming alternative that might fail: an app that sends mutations over a socket rather than HTTP would make the functional prompt's fetch-based replays (hro_interview_full, hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_*, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous) infeasible; however hireops_rules.md:21-23,78 specifies HTTP status semantics (401/403/404/409) for refusals, so HTTP actions are effectively public; residual tool-feasibility risk belongs to coverage/feasibility rows, not an inversion here. RUNTIME EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' Its entries (workspace.cjs 96410261..., results/workspace.json a424b50f..., results/server.log 6752f461...) re-hashed and match, and solution server.js/index.js/board.js hashes match the frozen task, but they are scripted golden observations only. No graded run of a golden vs mutated-weaker app pair exists, so the claim that the configured judge ranks a worse app below a better one is unmeasured. Per SKILL ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY 'Runtime and model evidence' (reward ordering record required), this row stays Not exercised with risk=true. No defect found in the static arrangement.
